$comment: Ground truth for sub-phase 3.6: where a block of text sits inside a shape, how far in from each edge, and which way it runs. Every number was read out of PowerPoint through TextRange2.BoundTop and BoundLeft, or off the EMF it exported. BoundWidth is recorded and not trusted - it overstates an advance by about 5pt. See docs/adr/phase-3-text/0032-anchors-insets-and-vertical-text.md.

questions.question: where a top-anchored, left-aligned block starts at zero insets

candidates.name: the frame edge
half the leading below it

questions.winner: the frame edge

questions.question: does each inset move the block by exactly its own value

candidates.name: the stated value, or 7.2/3.6 when absent
the stated value, or zero when absent
a symmetric 7.2 default on every edge
ignored

questions.winner: the stated value, or 7.2/3.6 when absent

questions.question: do rIns and bIns move a right-aligned or bottom-anchored block

candidates.name: the stated value, or 7.2/3.6 when absent
ignored

questions.winner: the stated value, or 7.2/3.6 when absent

questions.question: where the content box goes when the two insets exceed the frame

candidates.name: the midpoint of the two inset edges
the middle of the frame
split in proportion to the two insets
the near inset, unclamped

questions.winner: the midpoint of the two inset edges

questions.question: where each ST_TextAnchoringType puts the block

candidates.name: inside the inset box, with just and dist as bottom
inside the frame, ignoring the insets
inside the inset box, with just and dist as top
inside the inset box, with just and dist as centre

questions.winner: inside the inset box, with just and dist as bottom

questions.question: do just and dist spread the lines to fill the frame

candidates.name: no: the lines sit exactly where bottom anchoring puts them
yes: the lines spread

questions.winner: no: the lines sit exactly where bottom anchoring puts them

questions.question: how tall a block of n lines is, and how much of the last line leading it keeps

candidates.name: trimmed unless spcFirstLastPara
always a full advance
always trimmed
trimmed with no floor

questions.winner: trimmed unless spcFirstLastPara

questions.question: what @anchorCtr moves, and what an absent one means

candidates.name: on centres the block; absent is off
absent is on
it is the same as algn="ctr"

questions.winner: on centres the block; absent is off

questions.question: which axis @anchor governs once the text is turned, and from which edge

candidates.name: the stacking axis, from a start edge that depends on the vertical type
always vertically, whatever the text does
the stacking axis, always from the same edge

questions.winner: the stacking axis, from a start edge that depends on the vertical type

questions.question: which end of the line axis @algn="l" sits at

candidates.name: the axis start, which vert270 alone reverses
always the low coordinate
reversed by every vertical type

questions.winner: the axis start, which vert270 alone reverses

questions.question: which physical edge each inset holds under rotation

candidates.name: the insets stay on their own physical edges
the insets rotate with the text

questions.winner: the insets stay on their own physical edges

questions.question: which vertical types ask for the @-prefixed face

candidates.name: eaVert and mongolianVert only
every type but horz
never

questions.winner: eaVert and mongolianVert only

questions.question: what @vertOverflow draws when the text does not fit

candidates.name: a line is drawn only if it fits strictly; ellipsis replaces the first that does not
a line whose bottom lands exactly on the edge is drawn
ellipsis appends to the last line that fits
clip draws everything and relies on a clip region

questions.winner: a line is drawn only if it fits strictly; ellipsis replaces the first that does not

questions.question: does @vertOverflow change the height of the block

candidates.name: no: the block is laid out in full whatever is drawn
yes: it shrinks to what fits

questions.winner: no: the block is laid out in full whatever is drawn

questions.question: does a:br start a new bullet or advance an autonumber

candidates.name: no: one marker per a:p
yes: one marker per line

questions.winner: no: one marker per a:p

questions.question: does the line after a:br take the first-line indent

candidates.name: no: it starts at marL like any wrapped line
yes: it is a first line

questions.winner: no: it starts at marL like any wrapped line

questions.question: does a:br pay spcBef and spcAft

candidates.name: no: only a paragraph boundary does
yes: it is a paragraph boundary

questions.winner: no: only a paragraph boundary does

questions.question: does the a:rPr on an a:br set the height of the line it starts

candidates.name: no: the following run does
yes

questions.winner: no: the following run does

questions.question: how tall an a:p with no runs is

candidates.name: 1.2 x the a:endParaRPr size, times lnSpc
1.2 x the a:defRPr size when there is one
the a:endParaRPr size itself
zero: an empty paragraph takes no room

questions.winner: 1.2 x the a:endParaRPr size, times lnSpc

questions.question: how wide a column is, and how far apart two are

candidates.name: width = (frame - (n-1) x spcCol) / n, pitch = width + spcCol
pitch = frame / n, with spcCol inside it
width = frame / n, pitch = width + spcCol

questions.winner: width = (frame - (n-1) x spcCol) / n, pitch = width + spcCol

questions.question: does a bare a:bodyPr on a slide inherit from the layout and the master

candidates.name: yes, per attribute, from any level of the placeholder chain
no: a bare a:bodyPr means the schema default
from the layout only

questions.winner: yes, per attribute, from any level of the placeholder chain
